full_judgment: 22. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, submitted that circumstances as considered by the learned Sessions Judge are reasonable and believeable. He submitted that the story of causing injuries on the face and head of the victim through the window is absolutely an absurdity and standing on the 9" wide carnish such injuries on the face and head could not be inflicted from outside by the alleged fukni by any outsider. Several circumstances pointed out the guilt of the accused. He further submits that the conducts of the accused are destructive to the presumption of innocence. Failure on the part of the accused to give proper and reasonable explanation about the cause of murder will lead to a conclusion that in fact they committed this murder. Motive is to be gathered from the facts and circumstances of the case. Particularly, the dispute over Chalita as well as the fact that father-in-law of Chapa put trust on her instead of other sons and daughters and daughter-in-law of the house could not be ignored altogether. In a criminal case it is the duty of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused. But in certain cases and under certain circumstances the accused are also liable to give an explanation as to the cause of the occurrence. It is on evidence that other gates of the house of Khalilur Rahman were closed and it was not possible and there was no evidence also to show that some miscreants came from outside of the house, entered into the house through the doors and thereafter went upto the first floor of the building and went into the room of Chapa and killed her. From the defence case itself it appears that excepting the window where the khat of deceased Chapa was lying in no other way this occurrence could be done by any person from outside. So, Chapa was killed in her own room and other outsider could not enter into the room. The strong explanation of the accused who were the inmates of the house was that Chapa was killed by the outside miscreants standing on the 9" wide carnish and through the window with the help of a Fukni, that is, one and half cubit long G I pipe.
